questions.enonce_markdown:
The operating system performs several activities in a computer such as job scheduling in a pre-emptive and non-pre-emptive manner.

(a) What is job scheduling? (1 mark)

(b) Describe TWO scheduling strategies and say whether they are pre-emptive or non-pre-emptive. (3 marks)

(c) State three other functions of the operating system. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Job scheduling (1 mark).** Job scheduling is the activity of the operating system that decides which of the jobs (processes) waiting in the queue is given the processor, in what order and for how long, so that the CPU is kept busy and every job is served fairly and efficiently.

**(b) Two scheduling strategies (3 marks).**

- **First Come First Served (FCFS)** - the jobs are executed in the order in which they arrive in the queue. A job that has been given the CPU keeps it until it finishes (or asks for input or output), so no job can be interrupted. It is **non-pre-emptive**. Weakness: a long job at the front makes the short jobs behind it wait a long time.
- **Round Robin (time slicing)** - every job receives the CPU for a short fixed period called a time slice (quantum). When the slice ends, the job is interrupted, put at the back of the queue and the next job gets the CPU. Because the running job can be taken away from the CPU before it finishes, it is **pre-emptive**. It gives all users a fast response time.

(Other acceptable strategies: Shortest Job First - non-pre-emptive; Shortest Remaining Time First and priority scheduling with interruption - pre-emptive.)

**(c) Three other functions of the operating system (3 marks).**

- **Memory management** - allocating main memory to programs, protecting the memory of one program from another and freeing it when the program ends.
- **File management** - creating, naming, storing, copying, protecting, searching and deleting files and folders on the storage devices.
- **Device (input/output) management** - controlling peripheral devices such as the keyboard, the printer and the disk through device drivers, and handling their interrupts.

(Also acceptable: providing a user interface, security and user accounts management, error handling, networking.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Telemedicine and expert system are two applications that are common in the health domain.

(a) What is telemedicine? (1 mark)

(b) State two advantages of telemedicine. (2 marks)

(c) Describe ONE application of expert system in health. (2 marks)

(d) Describe ONE other application of the computer in health. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Telemedicine (1 mark).** Telemedicine is the use of telecommunication links and computers (internet, video conferencing, telephone, mobile applications) to give medical consultation, diagnosis, treatment advice or monitoring to a patient who is at a distance from the doctor.

**(b) Two advantages (2 marks).**

- Patients in remote or rural areas (for example villages far from a regional hospital) can consult a specialist without travelling, which saves time and transport costs.
- Specialists can share their opinion quickly and several doctors can discuss a case at the same time, which speeds up diagnosis; it also reduces crowding in hospitals and the risk of spreading infections.

**(c) Application of an expert system in health (2 marks).** A medical diagnosis expert system contains a knowledge base of facts and rules supplied by doctors and an inference engine. The doctor or nurse enters the patient's symptoms and test results and answers the questions asked by the system; the system reasons with its rules and suggests the most probable disease, with a degree of probability, and a possible treatment (for example MYCIN, which was used to identify bacterial infections and recommend antibiotics).

**(d) One other application of the computer in health (2 marks).** *Electronic patient records:* the details of every patient (identity, history, tests, prescriptions) are stored in a hospital database so that authorised staff can retrieve them instantly from any department, which avoids lost files and speeds up treatment.

(Other acceptable answers: computer-controlled scanners (CT, MRI, ultrasound), patient monitoring systems in intensive care, computer-assisted surgery, pharmacy stock control, appointment booking.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Briefly describe the following information systems

(a) Automation. (1 mark)

(b) GPS. (1 mark)

(c) Transaction Processing System. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Automation (1 mark).** Automation is the use of computers, machines and control systems to carry out a task or process automatically, with little or no human intervention (for example a robot arm on a car assembly line, or an automatic bottling plant).

**(b) GPS (1 mark).** The Global Positioning System is a satellite-based navigation system: a GPS receiver picks up signals from at least four satellites and calculates its exact position (longitude, latitude and altitude) and the time. It is used in car navigation, vehicle and fleet tracking, and mapping.

**(c) Transaction Processing System (1 mark).** A TPS is an information system that collects, processes, stores and retrieves the data of the day-to-day transactions of an organisation (sales at a supermarket till, bank deposits and withdrawals, payroll, ticket reservation), quickly and accurately, and keeps the records up to date.
